label: [optimized] order by id
description: Equality on order_id, served by order_id_1. Expected: index-supported and efficient.

label: [optimized] orders for customer
description: Equality on customer_id, served by the prefix of customer_id_1_total_cents_-1. Expected: index-supported and efficient.

label: [optimized] orders by region and category
description: Equality on both fields of region_1_category_1 with a limit. Expected: index-supported and efficient.

label: [optimized] top orders for customer
description: The $match equality and $sort follow the customer_id_1_total_cents_-1 key order, so the index returns documents already sorted. Expected: no in-memory sort.

label: [optimized] mark order shipped by id
description: Write targeted through order_id_1. Expected: index-supported and efficient.

label: [optimized] delete order by id
description: Delete targeted through order_id_1. Expected: index-supported and efficient.

label: [not optimized] orders by customer email
description: customer_email has no index, so a selective equality reads the whole collection. Expected: COLLSCAN with a selective filter and an index recommendation on customer_email.

label: [not optimized] orders by status and shipping city
description: Only status is indexed and it has six values, so status_1 reads about a sixth of the collection to find the few documents for one city. Expected: index with low selectivity.

label: [not optimized] flag gift orders by customer email
description: Write filtered on the unindexed customer_email. Expected: COLLSCAN for a single-document update.

label: [not optimized] biggest orders in region
description: region_1_category_1 finds the region, but its key order cannot provide total_cents order, so every matching document is sorted in memory. Expected: blocking (in-memory) sort; an index on { region: 1, total_cents: -1 } would remove it.

label: [not optimized] first order per region by notes
description: Sorts the whole collection on the large unindexed notes field before grouping. Expected: blocking sort that spills to disk once the sorted data exceeds the server sort memory limit (100 MB by default; about 100,000 documents with this collection definition).

label: [expected full scan] revenue by category
description: Reporting query with no filter: a collection scan is expected and an index would not help. Expected: unfiltered COLLSCAN reported as expected, not as an indexing problem.
